newsitem.title: USA: Pinnacle Micro names Campbell President.
newsitem.headline: Pinnacle Micro names Campbell President.

text.p: Pinnacle Micro Inc said Monday that interim President and Chief Executive Officer Lawrence Goelman had resigned and Kenneth Campbell had been appointed president and a director.
Campbell had been executive vice president-technology and general manager.
Goelman resigned on December 6, citing fundamental management differences with Scott Blum, a director. Goelman also resigned from the board, as did Blum.
Blum, a co-founder of Pinnacle, stepped down as vice president of marketing in October.

William Blum, also a co-founder, has returned to the board after retiring as president, chief executive officer and chairman in May. He, Scott Blum and the Blum Trusts have entered into certain "standstill" agreements with Pinnacle.
Finally, board member Charles Laverty has resigned his seat, and Chief Financial Officer Roger Hay has joined the board.
Also, Hans Imhof, co-owner of a data center engineering company called Datasphere, has joined the board.
A spokeswoman for Pinnacle said the company has no plans to name a chief executive officer at this time, but Campbell in his new role as president will assume the functions of a chief executive.

"Given Ken Campbell's critical role in delivering (company product) Apex, and reorganizing manufacturing and research and development, we have every confidence in his ability to lead Pinnacle Micro," Daryl White, chairman, said in a statement.
Pinnacle Micro's Apex 4.6 GB is a high capacity 5.25-inch removable, magneto-optical computer storage device. The drive began volume production in November.
"Apex shipments should ramp up significantly this week," White said. "We are filling backlog as fast as we can and building demand for the Apex product."
